title: Efficacy and safety of olanzapine, an atypical antipsychotic, in patients with schizophrenia: results of an open-label multicenter study in Japan.
text_summary: 这是奥氮平在日本精神分裂症患者中的首次临床研究，旨在探讨奥氮平的有效性和安全性。八十一名患者被纳入分析组。简短精神病学评定量表的结果显示，所有集群的基线均有所改善，包括阳性精神病症状（思维障碍），但也有阴性症状（无能）。该研究结果表明奥氮平是一种“非典型”抗精神病药。

Psychiatry and Clinical Neurosciences (2001), 55, 353–363


Regular Article
Efﬁcacy and safety of olanzapine,an atypical
antipsychotic,in patients with schizophrenia:Results
of an open-label multicenter study in Japan


           JUN ISHIGOOKA, md, phd, MITSUKUNI MURASAKI, md, phd,
          SADANORI MIURA, md, phd AND THE OLANZAPINE
           EARLY-PHASE II STUDY GROUP*
                Department of Psychiatry,Kitasato University School of Medicine,Sagamihara,Japan


Abstract       This ﬁrst clinical study of olanzapine in Japanese patients with schizophrenia was conducted to
                 investigate the efﬁcacy and safety of olanzapine. Eighty-one patients were included in the analy-
                    sis set. Mean modal dose for those patients were 9.4 ± 3.6 mg/day. For the primary efﬁcacy
              measure (Final Global Improvement Rating score), 14.8% of patients had remarkable improve-
               ment, 59.3% of patients had moderate improvement or better, and 86.4% of patients had slight
              improvement or better. Results from the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale showed improvement
              from baseline in all clusters including positive psychotic symptoms (thought disturbance) but
                 also against negative symptoms (anergia). The most commonly reported treatment-emergent
                 signs and symptoms with ≥10% incidence, were insomnia, weight increase, excitement, sleepiness,
             and anxiety. There was a low incidence of extrapyramidal treatment-emergent signs and symp-
                toms, and events reported were tremor (6.2%), muscle rigidity (3.7%), and akathisia (2.5%). The
              most commonly reported treatment-emergent laboratory changes, with ≥20% of incidence, were
                 prolactin elevations (24.3%) followed by increases in triglycerides (20.4%). However, mean pro-
                  lactin values tended to be normalized during the study. This study result suggests that olanzapine
                      is an ‘atypical’ antipsychotic.


Key words      atypical antipsychotic, clinical open-label trial, multi-acting receptor targeted agent, olanzapine,
                schizophrenia.
